key_insight: A higher polygenic risk score for coronary artery disease was associated with more severe coronary atherosclerosis on clinical CT angiograms, including higher CAD-RADS and CAC.
clinical_relevance: Genetic risk may help flag patients who are more likely to show greater anatomic coronary disease on routine CTA, potentially complementing imaging-based cardiovascular risk assessment.
method: 630 Penn Medicine BioBank participants with clinically obtained coronary CTA and genotype data
Calculated a published genome-wide PRS for angiographic CAD burden
Compared PRS with CAD-RADS severity and log-transformed CAC using Bayesian regression models
evidence_signal: LLM-extracted CAD-RADS and CAC values closely matched manual abstraction, and each 1-SD increase in PRS was linked to 20% higher odds of a more severe CAD-RADS category and higher CAC burden.
watch_item: This was a single real-world cohort with observed associations, so results need external validation before any clinical implementation.
paper_title: Association of a polygenic risk score with coronary atherosclerotic burden in clinical CT angiograms
